aboutH2: Renascent Paul J. Sullivan Centre: Live-in Treatment for Men in Whitby, Ontario
intro: Renascent is a not-for-profit rehab located in Whitby, Ontario. Renascent specializes in the treatment of substance, drug and alcohol abuse.

This listing is the Renascent Paul J. Sullivan Centre at 90 Colston Avenue in Brooklin, the village at the north end of Whitby. It is one of Renascent's three live-in centres and is for men and people who identify as male. Renascent has been running abstinence-based treatment since 1970, when Paul J. Sullivan and a group of people, many of them in recovery, founded it. The centre is accredited by the Canadian Centre for Accreditation, and the counsellors have their own lived experience of addiction and recovery.

pillars.title: A Country House in Brooklin
pillars.body: The Sullivan Centre is a big red brick house with a covered veranda, set on treed grounds on Colston Avenue in Brooklin. Renascent describes it as a serene, rural setting, and it feels like a home rather than a clinic. Inside there are bedrooms, a dining room, a kitchen, sitting rooms and a lecture room for groups. Out back there is a stone patio with a small fountain and woods behind it. The house is about an hour from downtown Toronto and a short drive from Oshawa and central Whitby.

pillars.title: Six Months of Continuing Care, Then Alumni for Life
pillars.body: If you come through the fee-for-service Complete Care program, the live-in stay is followed by six months of virtual Continuing Care. You meet once a week for relapse prevention work, with one-on-one and group counselling and assignments in between. After that you join the alumni community for good. Sullivan alumni meet in person at the house on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, and there is a monthly all-alumni meeting on Zoom. Family members can take the Family Program at Renascent's family health centre on Isabella Street in Toronto or online.

pillars.title: Counsellors Who Have Been There
pillars.body: Renascent says all of its counsellors have lived experience of addiction and recovery, and at the Sullivan Centre men attend group and individual counselling with male counsellors. The house is run by manager Justin Ryan, an addictions counsellor who also teaches in the Addiction and Mental Health program at Durham College. Dr. Dale Ryan, a physician with a background in addiction medicine and emergency medicine, is medical director for Sullivan and for Renascent's Madison Avenue Centre in Toronto. Registered psychotherapists and certified addiction counsellors make up the rest of the care team.

overview: Renascent's program is abstinence-based and built on 12-Step facilitation, with clinical and medical care added on top. Counsellors draw on cognitive behavioural techniques, DBT, reality therapy, person-centred and solution-focused therapy, mindfulness and art therapy. Trauma is handled through Seeking Safety, a program that helps people work on trauma and recovery skills at the same time. Every client sees a physician for a medical assessment and an individual withdrawal plan, and is assigned a counsellor for one-on-one sessions alongside daily groups.
serviceCaption: 11 services · as described on the centre's website
afterOverview: Days at the house follow a set weekly schedule of groups, counselling, meals and 12-Step work, and clients also go out to community 12-Step meetings. Renascent asks new clients to bring about $200 for transit to those meetings, one suitcase and one carry bag, their health card, photo ID and all current medications in their original bottles. Personal vehicles stay at home, and visits are restricted while you're in treatment.

location.heading: Renascent Paul J. Sullivan Centre in Whitby, Ontario
location.intro: The centre is a country house on Colston Avenue in Brooklin, the village at the north end of Whitby in Durham Region. Downtown Toronto is about an hour away by car, Oshawa and central Whitby are around 15 minutes south, and Peterborough is roughly an hour to the northeast.

faqIntro: Answers come from Renascent's own website, checked in October 2026. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.a: The fee-for-service Complete Care program costs $15,995 to $28,100, depending on whether you stay 28, 35 or 42 days and pick a single or double room. That price covers the live-in stay, withdrawal management support, six months of weekly virtual Continuing Care and the family programs. Renascent also runs a publicly funded 28-day program at no cost for people who qualify.

faqs.q: Is there free or publicly funded treatment at Renascent?
faqs.a: Yes. Renascent's 28-day live-in program is publicly funded for Ontarians 18 and older who meet the eligibility criteria. Wait times for funded beds are usually longer than for Complete Care, and the funded program doesn't include Continuing Care. Renascent says no one is turned away for lack of funds, so tell the team if cost is a problem.

Live-in treatment runs 28, 35 or 42 days. The publicly funded program is 28 days, while Complete Care can be 7 to 14 days longer and adds six months of weekly virtual Continuing Care after you leave the house.

Renascent gives withdrawal management support to everyone admitted to its live-in program, starting with a physician's assessment. Some people need a short stay with one of Renascent's healthcare partners to stabilize before they start treatment at the centre. This support is only for clients admitted to the live-in program.

faqs.q: Who is the Paul J. Sullivan Centre for?
faqs.a: The Sullivan Centre is for men and people who identify as male, and groups and individual sessions are led by male counsellors. Renascent's Graham Munro Centre in downtown Toronto is its centre for women. Renascent is LGBTQ2IA2S+ affirming and supports trans and non-binary clients in choosing the right centre.

faqs.q: Where is the centre and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at 90 Colston Avenue in Brooklin, part of Whitby in Durham Region. It's about an hour's drive from downtown Toronto and around 15 minutes from Oshawa, with Ajax, Pickering and Port Perry all within easy reach. Clients can't bring their own vehicle, so arrange a ride and ask the driver to wait until you've been cleared for admission.

Yes, Renascent has four centres across Toronto and Durham. The Madison Avenue Centre at 54 Madison Avenue in Toronto's Annex is its other men's house, and the Graham Munro Centre at 356 Dundas Street West is for women. The head office and family programs are at the Lilian & Don Wright Family Health Centre, 38 Isabella Street in Toronto.

Complete Care clients move into six months of virtual Continuing Care, with one session a week of relapse prevention, group and one-on-one counselling. Everyone who finishes treatment becomes part of the alumni community for life. Sullivan alumni meet at the house twice a month, and there's a monthly all-alumni meeting on Zoom.

faqs.q: Can I use insurance or financing?
faqs.a: Many private insurance plans cover addiction treatment, and Renascent will give you the paperwork your insurer needs. You can also finance the fee through Medicard, a personal bank loan or a health care credit card. Call 1-866-232-1212 to go over your options before you book.

faqs.q: Is there help for my family?
faqs.a: Yes. Renascent's Family Program includes a four-week Introduction to Family Care for adults, a Children's Program for ages 7 to 12 and a Teens' Program for ages 13 to 18, plus one-on-one counselling. Your loved ones can join even if you aren't in a Renascent program, and the family programs are funded by donors rather than government.

Call Renascent's Client Care and Access Centre at 1-866-232-1212 to start intake. After an assessment, the team matches you to a program and connects you with community support while you wait. Self-referral is all you need, and Renascent says rapid admission, often within 24 hours, is possible.
